P1.title: Paycheck
P1.summary: What an employer pays you for a pay period after taxes and deductions, and how to read the stub that comes with it.

P2.title: Gross vs net pay
P2.summary: Gross is what you earned. Net is what landed. Offers and loan applications use gross; your budget runs on net.

P3.title: Taxes withheld
P3.summary: Money sent to the government out of each check: federal, FICA, and state where it applies. A big refund was your money all along.

P4.title: Direct deposit
P4.summary: Pay sent straight to your account. Banks love it, which is why bonuses and fee waivers depend on it.

P5.title: Checking account
P5.summary: The account money moves through. Built for spending, not growing, so it pays almost nothing.

P6.title: Overdraft
P6.summary: Spending more than you have. The bank declines it or covers it and charges a fee, historically $30 to $35 each.

P7.title: Emergency fund
P7.summary: Cash kept separate for the car repair or the job gap. A concept, not a product, and nobody is selling it.

P8.title: Budget basics
P8.summary: Where the net pay goes each month, and the handful of methods people actually stick with.

P9.title: Side income & 1099
P9.summary: Getting paid without withholding: what you owe, when, and the quarterly payments nobody mentions.

P10.title: Capital gains tax
P10.summary: What you owe when you sell something for more than you paid, and why holding a year changes the rate.

P11.title: Tax-loss harvesting
P11.summary: Selling a loser to offset a winner's tax bill, and the wash-sale rule that trips people up.

C1.title: Savings account
C1.summary: An account for holding money. Pays interest, limits withdrawals, and at big banks pays close to zero.

C2.title: High-yield savings account
C2.summary: Same account, 10 to 50 times the rate, usually from an online bank with no branches to pay for.

C3.title: APY vs interest rate
C3.summary: APY is what you actually earn once interest earns interest. Always compare APY to APY.

C4.title: FDIC insurance
C4.summary: Government guarantee on deposits up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank. Covers deposits, not investments.

C6.title: Insurance basics
C6.summary: Health, renters, auto, term life: what each actually covers, what a deductible is, and how premiums are set.

C7.title: HSA
C7.summary: A health savings account with three tax breaks, and why some people treat it as a retirement account.

C8.title: Certificate of deposit
C8.summary: Lock money up for a set term for a set rate. The penalty for leaving early is the product.

C9.title: Money market fund
C9.summary: Looks like savings, is actually an investment fund. Not FDIC insured, and that difference matters.

C10.title: Inflation
C10.summary: Why cash loses buying power, how it's measured, and what it does to every other station on this map.

C11.title: The Fed & interest rates
C11.summary: Who sets the rate that moves your savings APY, your card APR, and your mortgage, and how to read a rate decision.

D1.title: Credit score
D1.summary: A three-digit guess at how likely you are to repay. Built from your history, sold by bureaus, and yours to dispute.

D2.title: Credit card
D2.summary: Borrow with each purchase, pay in full and owe no interest. Pay less and you're carrying one of the priciest loans around.

D3.title: APR
D3.summary: The yearly cost of borrowing. A 24% APR on $1,000 carried for a year is about $240.

D4.title: Buy now, pay later
D4.summary: Four payments over six weeks at checkout. The store pays the fee; you pay if you miss one or stack five plans.

I5.title: Compound growth
I5.summary: Returns on returns. Works for you in a fund and against you on a card balance. Starting early beats starting big.

D6.title: Student loans
D6.summary: Federal versus private, how interest accrues while you're in school, and what the repayment plans really cost.

D7.title: Car loans
D7.summary: Why the dealer asks about the monthly payment first, and how a longer term hides a higher price.

D8.title: Mortgage & PMI
D8.summary: The biggest loan most people take, the insurance you pay when you put less than 20% down, and what escrow is.

D9.title: Refinancing
D9.summary: Replacing a loan with a cheaper one, when the closing costs make it worth it, and when they don't.

D10.title: Debt payoff math
D10.summary: Avalanche versus snowball, minimum payments, and how long a balance actually takes to clear.

I1.title: 401(k) match
I1.summary: Employer money you only get if you contribute. Vesting decides when it's really yours.

I2.title: Roth vs traditional
I2.summary: Two tax timings for the same account: pay tax now or pay it later. A label, not a product.

I3.title: Index fund
I3.summary: One purchase, a slice of everything on a list. Cheap because nobody is paid to pick.

I4.title: Expense ratio
I4.summary: The fund's yearly fee, taken automatically. The one number known in advance, and it compounds against you.

I6.title: Brokerage account
I6.summary: The account that holds investments. Taxable, no limits, and how brokers earn on cash and order flow.

I7.title: Stocks vs bonds
I7.summary: Ownership versus lending. Why one swings more, and why most portfolios hold both.

I8.title: ETF vs mutual fund
I8.summary: Two wrappers for the same holdings: one trades all day, one prices once. What that changes for you.

I9.title: Target-date fund
I9.summary: A fund that rebalances itself as a year approaches. Convenient, and where high fees hide most often in 401(k)s.

I10.title: Diversification
I10.summary: Not putting it all in one place. What it protects against, and what it doesn't.

I11.title: Dollar-cost averaging
I11.summary: Investing a fixed amount on a schedule regardless of price. What it does to your average cost, and what it doesn't.

I12.title: Dividends
I12.summary: Cash a company pays holders, how it's taxed, and why a high yield can be a warning rather than a gift.

I13.title: Rebalancing
I13.summary: Selling what grew to buy what shrank, back to your target mix. How often, and why it feels wrong.

I14.title: Risk tolerance
I14.summary: How much drop you can sit through without selling. A behavior, not a questionnaire score.

I15.title: Valuation basics
I15.summary: P/E, market cap, and the other numbers on a quote page, and what each one can and can't tell you.

I16.title: Bond yields
I16.summary: Why bond prices fall when rates rise, what a yield curve is, and why people watch its shape.

I17.title: Leverage
I17.summary: Borrowing to invest or trade. Multiplies gains and losses alike, and the broker gets paid either way.

I18.title: Withdrawal rates
I18.summary: How much a portfolio can pay out each year without running dry, and where the famous 4% came from.

I19.title: Estate basics
I19.summary: Beneficiaries, wills, and why the form you filled out at the bank can override the will.

T1.title: Order types
T1.summary: Market, limit, stop. What each one promises, and when a market order costs you.

T2.title: Bid-ask spread
T2.summary: The gap between the buy and sell price. The quiet fee on every trade, biggest where volume is thinnest.

T3.title: Volatility
T3.summary: How much a price moves, how it's measured, and why it's priced into everything on this line.

T4.title: Technical vs fundamental
T4.summary: Charts versus financials. What each approach claims, and what the evidence says about both.

T5.title: Margin
T5.summary: Borrowing from your broker to buy more. The interest, the margin call, and who decides when you're sold out.

T6.title: Short selling
T6.summary: Betting a price falls by selling what you borrowed. Why the loss is unlimited and the borrow has a fee.

T8.title: Options basics
T8.summary: Calls, puts, premium, expiry. How most retail options expire worthless, and who collects the premium.

T9.title: Position sizing
T9.summary: How much to put in any one trade. The math that keeps one bad call from ending the account.

T10.title: Futures
T10.summary: Contracts on a future price, built-in leverage, and why they were invented for farmers, not traders.

T11.title: Backtesting
T11.summary: Testing a strategy on past data, and the overfitting trap that makes every backtest look great.

M1.title: Scams & red flags
M1.summary: Guaranteed returns, urgency, and payment by gift card. The patterns, so you recognize the next variation.

M2.title: Fintech "banks"
M2.summary: Apps that look like banks but aren't. Where your money actually sits, and what happens if the app fails.

M3.title: Robo-advisors
M3.summary: Automated portfolios for a fee. What they do, what the fee buys, and what a target-date fund does for less.

M4.title: AI money tools
M4.summary: How to evaluate one: who trained it, what it sells, whether it personalizes, and what it can't know about you.

M5.title: AI-generated finance content
M5.summary: How to spot it, why it hallucinates numbers, and the questions to ask before trusting any explainer, including this one.

M6.title: Crypto & stablecoins
M6.summary: Tokens, exchanges, wallets, and what a stablecoin is actually backed by. The custody risk nobody explains.

M7.title: Tokenized assets
M7.summary: Stocks and real estate on a blockchain. What's real, what's a wrapper, and who holds the underlying thing.

M8.title: Prediction markets
M8.summary: Betting on events, priced as probabilities. How the odds are set and why they're not quite forecasts.
